scored_cells.answer_excerpt:
To get your website cited by AI search engines — ChatGPT Search, Google AI Overviews / AI Mode, Perplexity, Bing Copilot, etc. — think less “trick the AI” and more **make your pages easy to crawl, trust, extract, and cite**.

There’s no guaranteed submission form that forces citations. The practical playbook is:

## 1. Make sure AI/search crawlers can access your site

If your content is blocked, it won’t be cited.

Check your `robots.txt` and CDN/WAF rules for:

- **Googlebot** — for Google Search and AI features.
- **Bingbot** — important for Bing Copilot and Microsoft AI experiences.
- **OAI-SearchBot** — OpenAI’s search crawler for ChatGPT search results.
- Avoid accidentally blocking crawlers with Cloudflare, bot protection, geo blocking, paywalls, login walls, or heavy JavaScript rendering.

OpenAI says publishers that allow **OAI-SearchBot** can appear in ChatGPT search results and track referral traffic from ChatGPT; it also distinguishes that from **GPTBot**, which relates to training opt-out controls. ([help-lb.openai.com](https://help-lb.openai.com/en/articles/12627856-publishers-and-developers-faq?utm_source=openai))

## 2. Do strong traditional SEO first

AI search engines still rely heavily on web search indexes, retrieval systems, and rankings. Google’s own guidance says SEO best practices remain relevant for AI features like AI Overviews and AI Mode. ([developers.google.com](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features?utm_source=openai))

**Generative Engine Optimization (GEO)** is the practice of making your brand, website, and content more likely to be discovered, understood, cited, or recommended by AI-powered answer engines such as ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Claude, Copilot, and Google AI Overviews.

It is similar to SEO, but instead of optimizing only for traditional search rankings, GEO focuses on helping **generative AI systems understand your expertise and include your content in answers**.

## GEO vs. SEO

| SEO | GEO |
|---|---|
| Optimizes for search engine rankings | Optimizes for AI-generated answers |
| Focuses on keywords, backlinks, technical SEO | Focuses on clarity, authority, citations, structured information, brand/entity recognition |
| Goal: get users to click your result | Goal: get AI systems to mention, cite, summarize, or recommend you |
| Content is written for search results pages | Content is written to be easily parsed, trusted, and reused by answer engines |

Good GEO usually builds on good SEO. You should not abandon SEO; you should extend it.

---

# How to do Generative Engine Optimization

## 1. Create content that directly answers real questions

Generative engines work well with clear, direct answers. Your pages should address the kinds of questions people actually ask AI tools.

Instead of only writing:

> “Our platform helps teams improve productivity.”

Write content that answers:

- What is the best software for remote team productivity?
- How does project management

**Short answer: yes, schema markup can help—but it’s not a direct “get cited by AI” switch.** Think of schema as **clarity infrastructure**, not a ranking/citation hack.

### How schema *can* help AI citations

Schema markup helps search engines and AI-assisted search systems understand:

- what the page is about,
- who authored or published it,
- what entities are mentioned,
- whether content is an article, product, FAQ, how-to, review, recipe, local business page, etc.,
- dates, pricing, ratings, organization details, and other structured facts.

Google’s structured-data docs frame schema primarily as a way to make pages eligible for rich results and help Google understand page content; Google recommends JSON-LD where possible. ([developers.google.com](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/intro-structured-data?utm_source=openai)) Bing also supports structured data as a way for publishers to annotate structured content for its crawlers. ([bing.com](https://www.bing.com/webmasters/help/marking-up-your-site-with-structured-data-3a93e731?country=69&utm_source=openai))

For AI citations specifically, schema may help **after your page is already discoverable and relevant** by making facts easier to extract. But the bigger determinants are usually:

1. **Can the AI/search system access and crawl the page?**
2. **Does the page clearly answer the query?**
3. **Is the content original, useful, and trustworthy?**

**Answer Engine Optimization — AEO —** is the practice of making your content easy for search engines, AI assistants, voice assistants, and generative search tools to understand, trust, extract, summarize, and cite as a direct answer.

Think of it as **SEO for “answer surfaces”** like:

- Google AI Overviews / AI Mode
- Featured snippets
- People Also Ask
- Bing Copilot
- Perplexity
- ChatGPT with search/browsing
- Voice assistants
- Knowledge panels

Google’s own guidance says that many “AEO/GEO hacks” are not separate magic; the core is still creating useful, crawlable, high-quality content that satisfies search intent, with clear structure and strong trust signals. ([developers.google.com](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide?authuser=4&hl=en&utm_source=openai))

## The simple version

Traditional SEO asks:

> “How do I rank this page?”

AEO asks:

> “How do I make my content the clearest, most trustworthy answer to a specific question?”

“AI SEO” usually means optimizing so your site can be **found, understood, cited, and trusted** by AI-powered search experiences like Google AI Overviews/AI Mode, Bing Copilot, Perplexity, ChatGPT browsing/search, etc. The short version: **good AI SEO is still strong technical SEO + genuinely useful, well-structured, authoritative content.** Google’s own guidance says foundational SEO best practices remain the basis for visibility in generative AI search features. ([developers.google.com](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide?authuser=4&hl=en&utm_source=openai))

## 1. Start with classic SEO fundamentals

Before doing anything “AI-specific,” make sure your site is crawlable and indexable.

**Checklist:**

- Submit an XML sitemap in Google Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools.
- Make sure important pages are not blocked by `robots.txt`, `noindex`, login walls, or broken canonical tags.
- Use clean URLs, descriptive titles, and strong meta descriptions.
- Build a logical internal linking structure.
- Improve Core Web Vitals, mobile usability, and page speed.
- Make sure every important page has a clear purpose and target query/topic.

Google’s SEO starter guidance still emphasizes crawlability, useful content, site structure, and structured data as important foundations.
